clue.text: See something wrong?

parts.note: read literally, to see something wrongly is to take its meaning amiss, not to witness a misdeed

explanation.surface: A question about spotting wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests witnessing a wrong; the cryptic reading is understanding something wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinterpret a remark is to perceive its meaning wrongly.

clue.text: Keep an eye on the screen

explanation.surface: Advice to watch the television.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for watching closely and a noun for a display unit attached to a computer.

clue.text: Work carelessly for member supporting winter sport

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece below holds up the one above, so the member comes after the sport

parts.note: skiing, so the sport's verb form ski
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone shirking work for a politician who backs skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp on effort is to do a job too economically, so carelessly.

clue.text: One rejected unfashionable actors

parts.note: out of fashion is simply out
the cast of a play is its actors

explanation.surface: A performer turned down from a troupe of has-been actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is someone cast aside by society.

clue.text: Talks about tree struts

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other here

parts.note: says, as a verb, means talks or speaks
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone chatting about a tree that holds up a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struts' looks like a noun for supports; it is the verb, to walk with a swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger along ostentatiously is to sashay, a showy walk.

clue.text: Rice often cooked for a meal

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Rice is frequently prepared to make a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Refection is an old word for refreshment or a light repast.

clue.text: Strange things formerly questionable to CIA

parts.note: ex- as in ex-wife means former

indicators.note: something questionable is doubtful or dodgy, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Odd items once of doubtful interest to the American intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'questionable' looks like a comment on the intelligence agency's interest; it signals the letters of 'to CIA' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are curiosities, unusual or foreign objects.

clue.text: Professional who might make an impression first!

parts.note: a dent is an impression in a surface
first abbreviated is 1st, read with the figure 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A tooth doctor who takes a mould of your teeth before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Dentists literally take impressions of teeth, which supports the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth doctor is a qualified practitioner, a member of a profession.

clue.text: Mine might be switched off!

parts.note: mine reads as the possessive pronoun, but it is an explosive device made safe by disarming

explanation.surface: Someone saying their device could be turned off.
explanation.definitionFit: A disarmed explosive has been made inactive and safe.

clue.text: Southern university p-people are sheep

parts.note: the stammered first letter mimics a stutter, so a synonym for people, folk, is given a stuttered first letter

explanation.surface: Stammering about southern university folk being sheep-like followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'p-p' stutter signals that the synonym folk is stammered too, giving F-FOLK. SUFFOLK is an English county and a breed of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk is a breed of black-faced sheep from eastern England.

clue.text: Little chef's basic requirement?

parts.note: Little Chef reads as a British roadside restaurant chain, but the clue means a small cook room's essential facility, a compact cooking area

explanation.surface: Asking what a roadside diner chain fundamentally needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Chef is a chain of British roadside restaurants; read instead as a small cooking space.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact cooking area, the diminutive of a culinary room, suits a small cook.

clue.text: Behave badly, but winning after some scenes

indicators.note: after places the winning piece behind the scenes piece

parts.note: an act of a play is a group of scenes
being up means ahead or winning

explanation.surface: Misbehaving, yet coming out ahead once a few scenes are over.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or play up, as a child or machine does.

clue.text: One doesn't need rules to reform china's art

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word and its s are used as fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ceramicist reworking the art of porcelain without needing rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel against all government rejects laws and authority.

clue.text: The distress of gold workers in dry environment?

indicators.note: the dry surroundings enclose the rest, so the two letters go round the others

parts.note: TT is teetotal, abstaining from drink
or is gold in heraldry
men can mean workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Gold miners suffering in a dry place.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is anguish, severe suffering of mind or body.

clue.text: Imagined collapsed veins before one got older

indicators.note: before puts the shuffled veins in front of the next piece
collapsed suggests the word veins has fallen apart into a new shape

parts.note: aged means grew older

explanation.surface: Someone's veins gave way before they grew old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' turns VEINS into ENVIS; 'one' is a link joining the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage is to picture something in the mind, to conceive of it.

clue.text: Point to nick across a vegetable

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass

indicators.note: the nick stretches across the A, enclosing it

parts.note: to nick or pinch is to steal

explanation.surface: Instructions to steal a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' and 'pinch' are both British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten cooked or raw.

clue.text: Referring to a couple of travel documents being short

parts.note: two visas, side by side

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the second of two visas

explanation.surface: Talking about two passport stamps that are too brief.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in relation to or compared with.

clue.text: Second eleven showing hesitation seeing their transport!

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players, a team
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A reserve side hesitates as they see the vehicle that will carry them.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat carries people across water, a means of travel.

clue.text: The way journeys are steps

parts.note: St is street, a way
rides are trips or journeys

explanation.surface: The route of a trip is made of footsteps.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are long paces, steps taken while walking.

clue.text: The weight of expectation?

parts.note: the phrase usually means pressure of hope, but read as a unit of weight associated with longing, since to long is to expect or yearn

explanation.surface: The burden of others' hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: A long ton is the imperial unit of 2,240 pounds used in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This imperial unit is a weight of 2,240 pounds, and to long for something is to yearn.

clue.text: Bringing a charge for accommodation

definitions.meaning: ... a complaint is formally submitting it

explanation.surface: Making an accusation in exchange for a place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means formally filing a complaint and also rented rooms where one stays.

clue.text: Pr agent served sea cucumber

indicators.note: served up suggests the letters are dished out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A publicity agent dished up a marine delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Trepang is a dried edible holothurian prized in Asian cuisine.

clue.text: Appreciated that trade user effected repairs

indicators.note: repairs rebuild things, so the letters are put back together in another order

explanation.surface: Grateful that a business customer fixed things.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cherished is valued highly.

clue.text: Maturity, not without heart, is a factor

parts.note: age means maturity or ripeness

indicators.note: the central letter of the word not is taken away

explanation.surface: Being old, though not heartless, is a consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'factor' here is a noun for a representative who acts on another's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a business representative or steward acting for someone, an intermediary.

clue.text: The defence offered by a former politician — singular!

parts.note: a Lib is a member of the old Liberal Party in Britain
I is short for singular, or the singular first person

explanation.surface: A one-off excuse given by an ex-politician.
explanation.definitionFit: This plea claims the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened.

clue.text: Theologian, covering a poor game, got hurt

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so DD goes outside the rest

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

indicators.note: poor suggests the word game is in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchman watching a feeble match was injured.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is 'poor' in the surface; in the wordplay that word is the signal to rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged means harmed or injured.

clue.text: Single friend accepted it was copy

parts.note: I is one, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: accepted means took in, so the friend holds the next piece inside

parts.note: mate is British slang for friend

explanation.surface: A lone friend accepted that the thing was a replica.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to reproduce another's style or action.

clue.text: Divers needing rigs replanning

indicators.note: divers in its old sense means various or diverse, so the letters scatter into another order

explanation.surface: Scuba divers needing their gear reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like people underwater; it is the archaic adjective meaning sundry, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Reworking a plan means drawing it up afresh.
